title: College Scorecard (U.S. Department of Education)
questions: median earnings ten years after entry by college
net price of public universities in a state
graduation rates of colleges in a state
student debt of graduates by school
most selective colleges by admission rate

key_only: more than a few requests an hour (DEMO_KEY is limited per IP address)

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md (they carry api.data.gov's public DEMO_KEY; replace it with your own free key if it answers OVER_RATE_LIMIT), save the JSON pages under the names shown, and upload them. Without the links: download the full data files from https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/ (Most Recent Institution-Level Data, CSV inside a zip) and upload the CSV; the CSV uses upper-case variable names (UNITID, INSTNM, MD_EARN_WNE_P10) listed in the data dictionary.

cache.why: Queries are small and the data are refreshed a few times a year; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: College Scorecard data are U.S. government works (Department of Education) in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the earnings and debt measures derive from federal administrative records and are published for public use.

citation: U.S. Department of Education, College Scorecard, {dataset}, api.data.gov/ed/collegescorecard, retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: Earnings, debt and net price cover only students who received federal aid (Title IV); a report must say so.

clarify: Which schools? All institutions, or only bachelor's-predominant (predominant_degree 3), and which ownership (public, private nonprofit, for-profit)?
Which cost measure: published tuition (in-state or out-of-state) or average net price after grants?
Earnings 6 or 10 years after entry? Both cover only federally aided students who are working.
